official_manualfamilyrelevant_sections Left Engine Failure and Subsequent Depressurization, Southwest Airlines Flight 1380, Boeing 737-7H4, N772SW
S006 · National Transportation Safety Board · 2019-11-19 · NTSB/AAR-19/03 · open (US government work)
Read: Executive summary p.viii incl. footnote 3; §1.3.1 Engine pp.11-14 incl. footnote 28; §1.3.2 Inlet pp.14-16 incl. footnote 35; §1.3.3 Fan Cowl pp.16-18 incl. footnote 37
Establishes: The CFM56-7B fan disk carries 24 Ti-6-4 wide-chord fan blades (~11 in chord, ~10.83 lb each) with aluminium platforms, inside an aluminium-alloy fan case, and the 737NG uses an asymmetric fan cowl and flat-bottom nacelle; a 1-stage HPT drives the 9-stage HPC and a 4-stage LPT drives fan and booster, rotating clockwise aft-looking-forward.
Limits: Accident engine was a -7B24; NTSB states CFM56-7B statements apply to all models (-7B18 to -7B27). Inlet/cowl are Boeing/UTAS airframe parts.

S007 · National Transportation Safety Board · unknown · NTSB DCA16FA217 · open (US government work)
Read: Analysis section pp.1-2
Establishes: Fan blade No. 23 of a CFM56-7B fractured at its dovetail root from a low-cycle fatigue crack after 38,152 cycles; fragments travelled forward into the inlet, most of which departed, and the blade material matched the specified titanium alloy.
Limits: Event report (accident date 27 Aug 2016); report publication date not shown on extracted pages; engine dash-number not stated in analysis.
